title: introduce-flashbridge-unified-attention-kernel-and-fused-rotary-rope-with-scheduler-guidance
author: Diego Alvarez
body: Motivation: We have multiple FlashAttention variants and several ad-hoc fused ops (rotary, rope) which complicate kernel selection and prevents smooth rollouts. This PR introduces a small compatibility layer (FlashBridge) that normalizes QKV layout and exposes a single fused rotary/rope operator so the runtime can pick the best back-end without per-model branching. It also adjusts the continuous-batching scheduler to expose a tunable adaptive window and integrates a lightweight KV-cache prefetch heuristic that reduces cold-KV misses for long-lived chat sessions. Changes are backward compatible and gated behind runtime flags (runtime.attn.flashbridge_enabled, runtime.scheduler.adaptive_window_ms, runtime.kv.prefetch_enabled). What this PR does: 1) Adds FlashBridge abstraction (C++): a thin shim that translates internal tensors to the memory/stride expectations of multiple FlashAttention implementations (FlashA V3, FlashA-lite, FuseX). 2) Implements a combined fused_rotary_rope operator (CUDA + CPU fallback) that performs rotary embedding application and rope swapping/interleave in a single kernel to reduce memory traffic. 3) Scheduler updates: adaptive continuous-batching window (ms-based), and a hot-key preservation policy that avoids coalescing requests with sticky KV sessions. 4) KV cache: prefetch heuristic that warms likely next-blocks for recurring chat sessions; configurable TTL. 5) Telemetry: new micro-metrics for kernel selection, per-model flashbridge fallbacks, and prefetch hit-rate. 6) Tests and perf harness: unit tests, integration smoke, and perf bench scripts. Checklist: - [x] Core abstraction implemented - [x] Fused operator implemented with CPU fallback - [x] Scheduler and kv-prefetch wired into runtime - [x] Unit + integration tests - [x] Benchmarks show net improvement - [x] Docs updated (internal perf guide). Links: design doc (internal): https://linear.app/redwood/board/ENG-1273/flashbridge-design, benchmark scripts: tests/perf/bench_attn.py. Rollout plan: feature gated, staged canary (10% traffic) then global rollout after 48h of no regression on p99 latency and error-rate.

review_comments: Avery Chen: overall design looks good. Please add a runtime flag to disable prefetch per-deployment (answered: added runtime.kv.prefetch_enabled).
Samir Patel: can you add microbench (seq512, seq2048) with both flash variants? (answered: added bench_attn.py variations and attached CSV).
Lena Koskinen: nit: document CPU fallback perf expectations in docs (answered: updated docs/perf/attention-upgrade.md).
Avery Chen: the kernel can be memory-bound for seq<=64, add an early-path to skip fuse (answered: added heuristic in kernel_selector.cc to prefer plain attn for very short sequences).
Samir Patel: CI flaked on e2e once, re-run passed (CI note).
merge_details: Merged by Avery Chen via squash; merge commit contains summarized changes and references ENG-1273. Canary rollout started after merge as described in the PR. No hotfixes required during canary window.
release_notes: Introduce FlashBridge (kernel abstraction) and a fused_rotary_rope operator to reduce memory copies and memory-bound stalls; adaptive continuous batching window and KV prefetch heuristic to improve throughput and p99 latency for long-lived chat sessions. Feature gated behind runtime flags. Expect ~12-28% token/s increase depending on sequence length and model; p99 latency reduction ~18% for seq512 in our bench harness.
notes_for_ops: Default rollout is disabled; enable with runtime.attn.flashbridge_enabled=true on Dedicated and Hosted canary clusters. Monitor metrics: runtime.attn.flashbridge.fallback_count, runtime.kv.prefetch.hit_rate, scheduler.adaptive_window.ms. Recommended canary: 10% traffic for 48 hours; revert flag if p99 latency increases or error-rate > baseline+0.1%.
related_work: See ENG-1338 for follow-up work to instrument kernel memory bandwidth counters and enable auto-tuning of the adaptive window. This PR lays the foundation for per-model quantization-aware kernel choices.
changelog_section: Performance: unified attention kernel layer (FlashBridge) and fused rotary/rope operator with scheduler integration; opt-in via runtime flags.
qa_coverage: unit + integration + perf smoke; manual canary validated against representative chat workload; regression tests added to CI.
